portion_doctrine: JUNK DETECTION + BOILERPLATE STRIP. Segments 1-10 of LIGHTING_SET_UPS_OG.docx contain approximately 85-90% transcribed YouTube video content about mood boards (fashion photography, creative direction, setup planning), Reddit discussions, and AI tool tutorials (Canva, Adobe Express, Google Gemini). <5% actionable lighting setup tactics exist. Core boilerplate: title pages, hashtag collections, UI navigation, repeated mood board methodology explanations, platform-specific tutorials. Real actionable content is sparse and fragmented across video transcripts.
operating_rules: Lighting reference: hard light vs soft light creates different shadows - hard light requires heavy makeup to prevent washout under direct exposure
Three-strobe portfolio setup: main light (optical spot modifier), background light (with gobo for texture), fill light (bounce off ceiling or bare bulb)
Mood board structure for film/photo: 5 pages minimum (title, lighting page, styling/hair/makeup, poses, vibes/energy)
Optical spot modifier with interchangeable lenses (Canon EF mount) allows variable spill coverage - kit lens for tight spots, 24-70mm for background coverage
Color grading workflow: raw processor (Capture One) used tethered on set to visualize post adjustments before final lighting tweaks
Gel application principle: magenta gels show most in shadow areas, not highlights
White/neutral walls mandatory for bounce-light fill technique; colored walls will shift subject color palette
Model direction via reference images outperforms verbal direction alone - visual mood board engagement increases model performance
tools: Westcott Optical Spot modifier (with lens projection system)
Canon EF mount lens library (24-70mm noted)
Canon R5 camera with RF 24-105mm lens
Google Gemini / Nano Banana (AI image generation)
prompts: Mood board title naming strategy: evocative concept names (Interstellar, Fuchsia Fantasy, etc.) prime team expectations and mental models
Reference gathering keywords: mix generalized terms (metallic, editorial, beauty) with specific photographer/model/magazine names to narrow Pinterest results
Lighting page copy template: use simple category labels (lighting, styling, hair/makeup, poses, vibes) for non-creative stakeholders
Model engagement prompt: show reference images of poses, expressions, movement vibe before shoot - reduces stiffness, increases authenticity
gates: Mood board must include descriptive labels for all team departments (makeup artist, stylist, gaffer) - vagueness causes misalignment
Lighting reference images must show 4-5 consistent examples (not 1-2) to establish pattern recognition for 'hard light,' 'soft light,' 'key light' concepts
Pre-production alignment gate: all departments (hair, makeup, wardrobe, lighting) review mood board and provide feedback before shoot day
content_ideas: Lighting modifier deep-dive: optical spot with interchangeable lens system as variable spill control mechanism
Gel stratification by light type: why gels appear differently in shadows vs highlights in three-light setups
Mood board as direction amplification tool - quantified impact on model performance vs verbal-only direction
Color grading as in-situ lighting adjustment - tethered workflow to test post-render before next setup
contradictions: Makeup weight vs light intensity tradeoff: hard light washes out makeup, so heavy makeup is required to compensate - but heavy makeup can photograph differently under soft light, requiring adjustment between light setups

Mood board minimalism vs specificity: brief mood boards (few images) give team creative freedom but risk misalignment; detailed mood boards (10+ images per category) reduce surprises but constrain team innovation
weird_gold: The 550 flash gun (camera flash, not strobe) mounted on shoulder with reflector balance mentioned in passing - suggests hybrid flash+natural light setup not fully detailed
Mention of 'shape board' separate from mood board - suggests layered pre-production reference system (color, texture, shapes, lighting, styling each on own board)
Gobo projection technique inspired by Valentino runway evening light - natural light reference applied to studio strobe (evening sunset light slices recreated via shaped gobo)
